title: Host health and history
summary: Inspect the host’s current checks and investigate changes, stops and listening gaps.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Host health shows the latest evaluated state of backups, anchors, disk, operating system and listeners, together with host information. Check now asks for another probe; requests less than a minute apart may show that the previous check is still recent.

Health history separates Application runs from State changes. Open a run to inspect its start, stop and any listening gap. State changes is a read-only history table with a check filter and continuation to older records.

The Health indicator in the application header opens this page. Dismiss notification can hide an App version notice across the current signed-in screens; the underlying version check and overall health remain visible here. Versions and updates describes acceptance of the detected running version and approval before a future update.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Read the individual check and its time before deciding what needs attention. Acknowledging a gap records review; it does not recover the results or other work that may have been missed.

Keep the application open when analyzer intake is needed. Follow the laboratory’s approved response to disk, clock, backup or listener findings, and record the relevant investigation in the offered workflow.

sections.title: If you cannot continue
paragraphs: A failed check needs its specific cause resolved. Use the related backup, instrument or recovery page when the finding points there. If the host cannot perform the check, retain the error details without patient information and involve the responsible operator.

pages.title: Host health
pages.purpose: Inspect current operational findings for this computer and its laboratory data.
pages.access: Available to signed-in users. Manage configuration is required for the checks that offer Attest.

fields.name: Overall
fields.meaning: Worst current evaluated health state.
fields.values: OK, Warning or Alert. Unknown individual checks count toward Warning.
fields.rules: Read-only; an overall state summarizes checks, not clinical readiness.

fields.name: Health indicator (application header)
fields.meaning: Summarize the current overall health on every signed-in screen and link to these details.
fields.values: Health: checking while loading; Health: OK, Warning or Alert after a successful read; Health: unavailable when the read fails.
fields.rules: Read-only; checked again every minute while the signed-in frame is open. Dismissing an App version notice does not hide this indicator or change the engine’s assessment.

fields.name: Operating system / Version / Edition / Architecture
fields.meaning: Identify the host platform.
fields.values: Values reported by the computer; a dash means not reported.
fields.rules: Read-only; not editable here.

fields.name: Web engine / App version / Data folder
fields.meaning: Identify the display engine, running software and local storage location.
fields.values: Reported engine/version and data-folder path.
fields.rules: Read-only; this page does not relocate data.

fields.name: Keep awake / Since / Problem code
fields.meaning: Sleep-prevention status and when it began.
fields.values: Keeping the computer awake; Not needed: no analyzer listener is active; Unavailable. Timestamp and problem code when supplied.
fields.rules: Read-only. Investigate Unavailable before depending on unattended analyzer intake.

fields.name: Check / State
fields.meaning: Identify an evaluated check and its result.
fields.values: OK: within the check’s limits. Warning: needs attention. Alert: needs action now. Unknown: app could not determine it. Attested: a person confirmed a supported manual check.
fields.rules: Read-only; checks appear with the most urgent first.

fields.name: Summary / Value / Limit
fields.meaning: Explain the observed condition and threshold used.
fields.values: Engine-provided explanation, measurement and configured threshold; dash where unavailable.
fields.rules: Read-only. Configurable thresholds come from Operations settings; checks with fixed engineering limits cannot be changed on this page.

fields.name: Observed / Next action
fields.meaning: When the check was evaluated and its suggested operational follow-up.
fields.values: Timestamp and provided action text.
fields.rules: Read-only. A recent page load is not necessarily a new probe.

fields.name: Attested
fields.meaning: Who manually verified the check and how long that attestation applies.
fields.values: Person, attestation time and valid-until time.
fields.rules: Read-only; manual attestations last 90 days in the current implementation.

fields.name: Note (Attest check)
fields.meaning: What was checked manually and how.
fields.values: PHI-free explanation up to 500 characters.
fields.rules: Required; retained in the audit trail. Attestation is offered only for disk encryption, OS support, web-engine smoke check, clock synchronization and power protection.

fields.name: Backup target
fields.meaning: Whether an active backup target is configured.
fields.values: Read the check’s current State, Summary, Value and Limit.
fields.rules: Read-only evaluation; follow its Next action. Manual attestation cannot override every kind of failed check.

actions.name: Check now
actions.availableWhen: Signed in; no more than once per minute.
actions.result: Refreshes evaluated checks; an early request explains that a recent check already exists.

actions.name: Open check / Previous / Next / Close
actions.does: Inspect the full explanation, observed values and available attestation.

actions.name: Attest
actions.does: Record manual verification of a supported check.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration and a check that offers Attest; required note.
actions.result: Saves who attested and the validity period; it does not perform the hardware or external check.

actions.name: Health history
actions.does: Open startup, shutdown and health-state records.
actions.result: Navigates to Application runs and State changes.

actions.name: Health indicator / Versions and updates
actions.does: Open Host health from the application header, or open the installed-version and update records from an App version notice.
actions.availableWhen: Signed in; the Versions and updates notice link is present while its warning or alert notice is shown.
actions.result: Navigates to the relevant evidence without accepting a version, approving an update or changing the health finding.

actions.name: Dismiss notification (App version notice)
actions.does: Hide the app-wide App version notice for the current signed-in view.
actions.availableWhen: An App version warning or alert notice is visible. Recovery reconciliation has no dismiss control.
actions.result: The check and overall health remain visible. A changed version or warning, recurrence after resolution, or a recreated signed-in view shows the notice again. See Versions and updates for acceptance and approval; dismissal records neither.

actions.name: Cancel (Attest check)
actions.does: Close the attestation form without saving its note.
actions.availableWhen: The attestation command is not running.
actions.result: No attestation is recorded. Return to the check and reopen Attest when ready.

restrictions: Unknown is not healthy evidence. Read each finding and its observation time.
A health check does not repair the underlying cause; use the relevant backup, instrument, recovery or operating-system procedure.
Closing the App version notice does not acknowledge, approve or accept the version. Recovery reconciliation continues to show its notice and enforce its release, delivery and billing restrictions.
workflow: Inspect Overall and the most urgent individual checks.
Open a check and read its value, limit, time and next action.
Resolve the specific cause, or manually verify an attestable condition and record the evidence.
Use Check now after correction, respecting the one-minute interval.

troubleshooting.problem: Checked less than a minute ago
troubleshooting.recovery: Review the latest results and retry after the minimum interval; this message is expected rate limiting.
Resolve the measured condition through its owning workflow. Only supported manual checks offer attestation.
Use the visible retry action and retain the error/correlation ID; unavailable health data does not prove the system is healthy.

troubleshooting.problem: Health still warns after closing the App version notice
troubleshooting.recovery: Dismissal only hides the notice. Open Versions and updates, inspect Running version, complete the laboratory’s checks and use its acceptance action when available. An unapproved later version also needs approval followed by a restart under that approval.

troubleshooting.problem: The App version notice appeared again
troubleshooting.recovery: The version or warning changed, a resolved warning recurred, or the signed-in view was recreated after a lock, sign-in or restart. Read the current finding; the previous dismissal did not resolve it.

pages.title: Health history
pages.purpose: Investigate application runs, listening gaps and changes in health findings.
pages.access: Available to signed-in users. Perform analysis is required to acknowledge a listening gap.

fields.name: Application runs / State changes tabs
fields.meaning: Switch between process sessions and changes in check states.
fields.values: Application runs (default); State changes.
fields.rules: Application runs loads 200 at a time; State changes loads 100. Load older runs or Load older state changes continues until all matching history is reached. Sorting covers loaded rows only.

fields.name: Started / Stopped / How it stopped
fields.meaning: Timing and manner of an application run.
fields.values: Recorded times; Closed normally, Quit despite warnings, other supplied code or dash when unknown.
fields.rules: Read-only; missing stop time is not automatically a clean stop. Recorded start time orders the display, with stable record identity breaking ties; clock changes can make this differ from the actual sequence of starts.

fields.name: App version / Web engine
fields.meaning: Software active during the selected run.
fields.values: Recorded version/engine, or dash if unavailable.
fields.rules: Read-only; compare with the current host version when investigating regressions.

fields.name: Gap before start / Clock gaps
fields.meaning: Recorded interruptions or forward-clock gaps associated with a run.
fields.values: Durations in seconds, or dash when absent.
fields.rules: Read-only. A stop longer than 60 seconds is a listening gap; clock gaps follow the configured threshold.

fields.name: Previous stop unclean
fields.meaning: Whether the prior run ended without a recorded normal stop.
fields.values: Yes or No.
fields.rules: Read-only; investigate alongside gap times.

fields.name: Gaps acknowledged
fields.meaning: Who recorded review of the run’s open gaps and when.
fields.values: Person/time or dash if not acknowledged.
fields.rules: Read-only; acknowledgement is separate from recovering missing results.

fields.name: Note (Acknowledge listening gap)
fields.meaning: Investigation performed and results needing resend or reconciliation.
fields.values: PHI-free explanation up to 500 characters.
fields.rules: Required; retained in the audit trail.

fields.name: Check (State changes filter)
fields.meaning: Select the health check whose state history is shown.
fields.values: All checks, or a check reported by the current installation.
fields.rules: Optional; defaults to all.

fields.name: Check / State / Detail code / Observed (State changes)
fields.meaning: Identify a recorded check transition and its reason.
fields.values: Check label, health state, machine-readable detail code and time.
fields.rules: Read-only table; rows have distinct retained identities even when their check, state and observation time match. Recorded observation time orders the display; equal times and clock rollback do not establish causal sequence. State changes do not open an editable record.

actions.name: Open application run / Previous / Next / Close
actions.does: Inspect run timing, software and gap facts.
actions.availableWhen: The run is loaded in history, or an exact run is linked from a work queue independently of the current history page.

actions.name: Acknowledge listening gap / Acknowledge
actions.does: Record completed investigation of the run’s outstanding gaps.
actions.availableWhen: Perform analysis and a run needing acknowledgement; required note.
actions.result: Marks the currently outstanding start/clock gaps acknowledged and records the review.

actions.name: Check filter / Clear filters
actions.does: Narrow or restore the health state-change history.

actions.name: Host health breadcrumb
actions.availableWhen: Above the title, as Host health › Health history.
actions.result: Shows the latest evaluated health state.

actions.name: Load older runs / Load older state changes
actions.does: Append the next page of matching retained records.
actions.availableWhen: A further page is available; the button shows progress while loading.
actions.result: Older entries remain reachable without changing the filters or recreating records.

actions.name: Refresh
actions.does: Reload the selected history and, for Application runs, the exact selected record.
actions.availableWhen: Either history tab; current query errors also offer recovery.
actions.result: Updated state and acknowledgement facts replace the prior read. A read failure remains visible and does not imply no history exists.

actions.name: Cancel (Acknowledge listening gap)
actions.does: Close the acknowledgement form without saving its note.
actions.availableWhen: The acknowledgement command is not running.
actions.result: The gap retains its actual acknowledgement state. Complete the investigation before reopening the action.

restrictions: Acknowledging a gap does not reimport analyzer results or recreate work lost while the application was not listening.
Recorded times and stable identities order the history for browsing. They do not reconstruct causal chronology when older evidence is ambiguous.

After upgrading legacy health history, the next actual evaluation records a fresh observation for each check before resuming state-change deduplication. Original observations are not reordered or rewritten; the new baseline can repeat a visible state.
workflow: Inspect Application runs around the incident.
Open the relevant run and review gaps, unclean-stop status and software versions.
Check analyzer records and reconcile missing work before acknowledging with a specific note.
Use State changes to correlate the incident with a check’s changing state.

troubleshooting.problem: An older run or state change is not yet shown
troubleshooting.recovery: Load older entries until the desired period is reached. A work-queue run link retrieves its exact record independently. If that record is unavailable, refresh or return to the queue; retain the error details for investigation.
Confirm the run still has an unacknowledged gap and that your account can perform analysis; do not acknowledge before investigation.
